Command: Do not reap the aftergrowth in the sabbatical year
Summary: In the sabbatical year, the aftergrowth — what grows of itself — is not to be reaped as a harvest.
Commandment: Do not reap the aftergrowth in the sabbatical year.
Application: Aftergrowth in the sabbatical year is free food, not a crop: it may be eaten by the household, the servant, the stranger, and the beasts, but not reaped as a harvest. The distinction between eating and harvesting protects the year's rest.
Purpose: To prevent permanent destitution and permanent debt in Israel (Leviticus 25; Deuteronomy 15). In the sabbatical year, that purpose takes the form of leaving the aftergrowth unreaped.
Function: In the sabbatical year, the aftergrowth — what grows of itself — is not to be reaped as a harvest. The civil order shows here — a rule keeping the common life honest and whole. It set out to prevent permanent destitution and permanent debt in Israel (Leviticus 25; Deuteronomy 15). It did not address a particular evil the way a civil law does; its work was rest, rhythm, and trust, not restraint.
